subject: QBR: infrastructure cadence, governance, and contingency alignment
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>, Emily Rogers <emily@pulseai.com>
Cc: 
Date: Thu, 10 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: QBR: infrastructure cadence, governance, and contingency alignment

Team / Emily —

Ahead of next week’s QBR readout with GTM, I want to align on the infra and engineering points we need to present: current roadmap status for the hosted and dedicated stacks, launch timelines for the PulseAI pilot, and a concise set of delivery risks plus mitigation options. Goal: a two-slide summary we can show execs and PulseAI that highlights impact and asks.

Please review the attached infra snapshot (v2) and contingency matrix. High-level asks:
- Karthik: confirm gating items for Dedicated capacity (network isolation + cert rotation) and any remaining ETA changes by EOD Friday.
- Laura: provide a one-paragraph summary of QA/regression posture against the pilot prompts and any known model-behavior risk.
- Marcus: surface any infra-level single points of failure (capacity, DB migrations, KMS) and a recommended fallback for each.
- Tessa: prep a short runbook snippet for a degraded-serving scenario (fallback model + routing policy) we can show.

Emily — appreciate if you can confirm whether the PulseAI security questionnaire was updated with your procurement team; if not, we should include an ask for their timeline in the QBR.

Timing: I want draft slides by Monday 09/13 10:00 PT so we can iterate before the pre-brief.

Thanks,
Vanessa
Vanessa Ortiz | Head of Customer Success & Partnerships
Redwood Inference
attachments: qbr_infra_snapshot_v2.pdf, launch-contingency-matrix.xlsx
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>, Emily Rogers <emily@pulseai.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Sep 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: QBR: infrastructure cadence, governance, and contingency alignment

Vanessa — quick update inline: 

- Dedicated capacity gating: network isolation is in final validation (ETA 9/15), certificate rotation tooling is complete but needs one more integration test with PulseAI keys (we're coordinating with their security team). If integration test slips, we can provide a short-term SAR (shared audit reporting) until rotation is finished.
- ETA changes: we are still targeting the dedicated pool to be available for the pilot by 9/20; putting a buffer on the first week of the pilot for warm-up.

Risk callouts:
1) KMS automated key rotation failures (rare but high impact) — mitigation: temporary HSM passthrough + extended logging, Fallback window: 30m estimated recovery.
2) Inter-region failover timing under heavy KV-cache load — mitigation: throttled warm-start and pre-warmed cache on standby nodes.

I’ll attach a short note with the KMS fallback steps.

—Karthik
Head of Infrastructure — Redwood Inference
From: Emily Rogers <emily@pulseai.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 11 Sep 2026 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: QBR: infrastructure cadence, governance, and contingency alignment

Thanks Vanessa — we got the infra snapshot and the security questionnaire draft. Procurement is still reviewing; Samir in our procurement team will confirm timeline (cc'd once I have it). A couple of asks from Pulse:
- Can Redwood provide the expected token-latency profile during peak and degraded modes (numbers, not just qualitative)? My engineering lead will want that on the QBR slide.
- For the pilot we need a documented data deletion policy (retention + audit log visibility) for the dedicated pool.

I can confirm by Monday whether procurement will sign off before the QBR. If not, we should surface an SLA/credit ask and an internal rollback window during the meeting.

Best,
Emily Rogers
Director, Platform Integrations — PulseAI
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>, Emily Rogers <emily@pulseai.com>
Date: Fri, 11 Sep 2026 13:58:00 -0700
Subject: Re: QBR: infrastructure cadence, governance, and contingency alignment

Vanessa / team — QA snapshot (summary):
- Regression coverage: pilot prompt set = 82% pass; 6 prompt families flagged for hallucination risk under long-context tests. Details in the attached regression note (not attached to this thread to limit size).
- Known behavior risk: conditional prompting with large persona context can increase token churn and latency outliers. Mitigation: enforce a 1,024 token hard cap for context during the pilot, and use server-side truncation with a warning to PulseAI on content loss.

I’ll put a one-paragraph slide for the QBR deck that summarizes these items and references the contingency matrix.

—Laura
VP, Product — Redwood Inference
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>, Emily Rogers <emily@pulseai.com>
Date: Sat, 12 Sep 2026 17:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: QBR: infrastructure cadence, governance, and contingency alignment

Quick runbook highlights and SLO asks for the QBR slide (draft):
- Degraded-serving scenario (cause: backend KV cache miss storm): route to lighter quantized model variant (q4_kv) + enable 10% sampling to preserve quality signal. Fallback latency expectation: +120–250ms per request.
- DB migration window: we will require a 30-minute maintenance window; ask: please confirm PulseAI can accept this window during pilot ramp days (we'll use traffic shaping).
- Single points: KMS (mitigation: HSM passthrough), shared metrics pipeline (mitigation: log-forwarder local buffering).

I uploaded the contingency matrix to the drive folder and updated the sheet with capacity numbers. Link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1QBR-Infrastructure-Pack

I can convert these bullets into the slide deck and send a draft by Monday 10:00 PT.

—Marcus
Director of Platform Reliability — Redwood Inference
